contract: Exclusive native OPEN Worker attach; authenticated TLS must be outside its driver. Success consumes one original native owner, returns one ordinary peer in UPGRADING; false preserves binding/owner/output. Original TLS session/config owner remains alive.
Strict Core GET/101/key/Accept/subprotocol/fields; preserve coalesced WS suffix; no JSON/business before checked101, no redirects/retries/downgrades/replay. Both endpoint roles, native TCP/TLS.

One original factory-entry setup clock spans copy, queue, parse, shared authorization, output and handoff. Queued call/batch/notify retain entry clocks. HTTP/auth rejection, malformed negotiation and timeout retain exact HTTP_ERROR/PROTOCOL/TIMEOUT with NOT_SENT.

Route/method/version/Host/Origin policies, bounded extras, pretransfer injection rejection,401 challenge,400/403/404/405/426/431/500/503 and native close. Auth executes on existing shared Server quotas/executor with owned immutable header/context, poll-only cancel/original deadline. Noncooperative work delays actual retirement.

Legacy validated attach remains available; selecting HTTP does not change its config/info layout. Duplex Close accepts setup TIMEOUT and HTTP_ERROR, preserves first reason/delivery/operation clocks, and joins physical work.
resources: Current Windows/Linux x64: existing WS config520 and info680 bytes unchanged; private peer1672 to1768 bytes when selecting HTTP, a96-byte fixed increase. Additional per-work pointer/state branches are not a measured performance result.

Cold control/field views/outgoing bytes are bounded and erased/released after handoff and old binding tail. Header16KiB/128 fields, write64KiB, extras32/16KiB, auth context16KiB hard caps. Native IO and existing Duplex limits remain separate.

Only the exceptional unpublished-read/full-record-growth case adds a bounded16KiB head cache. It consumes through CRLFCRLF, preserves suffix and counts actual preview copies. Shared auth copies one bounded head snapshot and context into the peer; ordinary handler admission retains its existing context copy. No zero-copy or zero-overhead claim.

Actual constructor original-budget ladder verifies false-output/native/credit rollback and zero live allocations after final physical joins. Async cache/auth/handoff fault and broader OOM/fuzz coverage are still incomplete; no quota reset or substitute runtime is introduced.
verification: 74 Windows/76 WSL primary C executions:5 modular/example,3 single,9 forced-backend/example,1 full Duplex,6 static/shared/declarations,2 legacy HTTP-off,38 independent sessions and10 repeated TLS byte-split sessions per host; WSL adds2 TSan. WSL focused/backends/Duplex/legacy/interop uses ASan+UBSan+leak halt; packages are O2 unsanitized. ABI probes, package smoke checks and7 Python gates per host are additional. All selected final receipts use the same final source map.

The first native TLS prefix fixture reproduced a valid9-byte buffered header failing ReadMore STATE with no original Read callback. Bound the exceptional cold cache; keep original gap source/binary/log and final constructor OOM/owner checks.
A client setup timeout exposed Duplex Close rejecting TIMEOUT; fix valid close reasons and add a full12-shape delivery/close regression.

Independent finish notification was not an execution acknowledgement; replace it with a checked RPC final barrier before WS/TLS close. Remove a printf use after future destruction by snapshotting scalars first.
Independent rejection fixture explicitly aborted after its unsent call became terminal, which can truncate an orderly HTTP response. Wait for physical rejection retirement before explicit Close.

A coalesced101/first Ping on byte-split native TLS exposed duplicate ReadMore: ParseTls already requests growth and may synchronously grow before returning MORE. A second request could survive across a complete head with a suffix and block owned exchange. Remove the duplicate; rerun final focused/single/packages/TSan/matrices/repeats.
